candidates.summary: The Trump administration filed an emergency Supreme Court appeal seeking to segregate about 20,000 California mail ballots from voters it suspects may not be citizens while their eligibility is checked. California officials say the federal list is unreliable and includes citizens; lower courts rejected the request, warning that it could disrupt the November 3 midterm election and disenfranchise eligible voters.
candidates.title: Trump administration asks Supreme Court to segregate disputed California ballots

candidates.summary: Uganda's military announced that it had begun a phased withdrawal of its peacekeeping troops from Somalia under a bilateral agreement with Somali authorities. A military spokesperson said the first contingent had returned to Uganda and that thousands remained deployed; all Ugandan troops are expected to leave by the end of 2027.
candidates.title: Uganda announces phased withdrawal of troops from Somalia

candidates.summary: Iran said its seven-step proposal for reopening the Strait of Hormuz and resuming nuclear negotiations with the United States could be condensed into two days if Washington met its conditions. Iranian officials said contacts through mediators remained active, but the latest Qatari-mediated discussions had ended without a breakthrough.
candidates.title: Iran outlines shortened plan for reopening Strait of Hormuz
candidates.geography: Iran; United States; Qatar; Strait of Hormuz

candidates.summary: World Health Organization Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said reported attacks in northern Ethiopia had killed civilians, including children, and warned that the region's health system was nearing collapse. Tedros did not give dates or casualty totals for the cited attacks or identify the perpetrators; he said insecurity was obstructing medical deliveries.
candidates.title: WHO chief warns northern Ethiopia health system is nearing collapse
